title: 8 Organic Baby Food Brands To AVOID (And The 5 That Are Actually Safe)
summary: List video ranking baby food brands by heavy-metal findings from a 2021 congressional report, arguing organic labels and premium prices gave no protection against lead, arsenic and cadmium.

assertions.quote: A green badge on a jar that contains the same contaminants as the cheapest conventional product on the shelf.

verdicts.note: Organic rules govern farming inputs, not soil heavy metals; congressional and consumer testing found organic baby foods no lower in lead and arsenic.
Organic crops had lower but nonzero Cd, and the meta-analyses found no difference in arsenic or lead between organic and conventional crops.
Meta-analyses found no difference between organic and conventional crops in lead, mercury or arsenic, and the cadmium advantage is limited to cereals.

7 CFR 205.203 only requires managing inputs so they do not add to heavy-metal contamination, and the 205.671 residue exclusion covers prohibited substances; the excerpt sets no heavy-metal limit for organic food.

assertions.quote: The heavy metal crisis in baby food is driven largely by rice and root vegetables that absorb arsenic, lead, and cadmium directly from soil.

verdicts.note: Rice takes up arsenic from flooded paddies far more than other grains, which is why FDA set a specific limit for infant rice cereal.

assertions.quote: Earth's Best proved that an organic label can function as decoration.
The company charges 30 to 50% more than conventional brands

verdicts.note: Retail price surveys commonly find organic premiums from about a fifth to double the conventional price, varying widely by item.
